what: Terreno Realty is a REIT that buys industrial property in six coastal US markets only: Northern New Jersey and New York, Los Angeles, the San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle, Miami and Washington DC. It buys infill locations close to dense populations rather than large warehouses on the outskirts.
customers: Distributors, logistics firms, construction suppliers and service businesses that need to be physically near a big city's customers, plus some trucking and container-handling operators who lease open land.
money: Leases on infill warehouses, light industrial buildings, transshipment facilities and improved land.
moat: Land close to the centre of coastal cities is effectively irreplaceable: it is zoned, scarce, and no one is building new warehouses there. Tenants who must reach city customers within an hour have very few alternatives, which gives Terreno unusual pricing power at renewal.
risks: The shares trade at about 13.8 times sales and 25.3 times EV/EBITDA, a notable premium even among industrial REITs.
Concentration in six markets means a downturn in Southern California or Northern New Jersey has an outsized effect.
Southern California industrial rents have fallen from their peak after a period of extraordinary increases.
Growth depends on buying properties, and in a competitive market paying up for assets lowers future returns.
Debt is about $943.3M against only $25.0M of cash.
opportunities: Revenue has grown strongly every year shown, from $221.9M in 2021 to $476.4M in 2025.
Leases signed years ago are far below current market rents in these markets, so renewals produce large step-ups.
The portfolio's locations cannot be replicated, which supports value even when the broader warehouse market softens.
Seventeen analysts average a $73.65 target, about 14% above the current price.
watch: Rent change on new and renewed leases. In a REIT whose premium rests on scarce locations, the re-leasing spread is the proof that the scarcity is real.
